members.note: Not: does not, will not, does not want to; the only negation before an adjective (不贵).

examples.text: 不，这是她！
汤姆不喜欢我。
谁不知道这件事？

members.note: Did not, has not: a past event or a change not reached yet; 没有 also means do not have.

examples.text: 我没吃饭。
她没有真朋友。
这本书没那本大。

groups.text: 不 negates the present, the future, habits, wishes and adjectives; 没 (没有) negates what happened or a change not yet reached, and 有 itself. 不 + Verb: does not, will not; 没 + Verb: did not, has not. 是, 会 and 应该 take only 不.

members.note: A learned skill (会游泳), or a prediction (明天会下雨).

examples.text: 她会说法语。
今晚会下雪吗？
他们会说英语。

members.note: Ability or capacity, or circumstances that allow it (今天能来).

examples.text: 他对我说，我也能说。
在电话里，我能听它叫。
他很能说，他们都喜欢他。

members.note: Permission; also that something is possible or acceptable.

examples.text: 我可以多来点牛奶吗？
他们说，我可以看他们怎么做。
我说下雨了，我们可以读一些书。

groups.text: All three can be translated as can. 会 is a skill that was learned, or a likely future event; 能 is ability, or conditions that make an action possible; 可以 is permission. 不会 means does not know how, or will not happen; 不能 and 不可以 both refuse.

members.note: After an adjective (快一点儿) or before a noun (一点儿水); 一点儿也不 means not at all.

examples.text: 给我一点钱。
请说慢一点。
他比我高一点儿。

members.note: Before an adjective or a verb of feeling, mostly for something unwanted (有一点儿累); also 有点儿.

examples.text: 出发以前，我心里有点儿担心，因为我从来没有当过老师。
这里有点吵，请你讲话大点声。
期待是期待，而感到有点麻烦。

groups.text: Both mean a little, but sit on opposite sides of the word. 有一点儿 + Adjective comes before it and usually signals something unwelcome. Adjective + 一点儿 comes after it to compare or soften, and 一点儿 + Noun is a small amount.

members.note: Or, in a choice question (你喝茶还是咖啡？); 还是…吧 means had better.

examples.text: 这是猫还是狗？
那是只猫还是只狗？
你觉得这本书的哪个译本比较好？法语的还是英语的？

members.note: Or, in a statement: either option is fine (今天或者明天).

examples.text: 回来以后，我们在房间里看电视节目，或者喝啤酒。
我想说不关你是老人，年轻人或者小孩子，也不管你的工作是什么，你一定要愉快地开始新的一天，也就是早晨！
如果水果有一点坏，她会主动告诉顾客，或者便宜一些卖。

groups.text: Both mean or. 还是 offers a choice the listener has to make, so it belongs in questions: A 还是 B? 或者 joins options in a statement where either one will do: A 或者 B. In a question already ending in 吗, use 或者.

members.note: Before a time or an event; often the moment just before (睡觉之前).

examples.text: 我父亲没之前好了。
明日之前必须把工作做完.
在你去睡觉之前不要喝啤酒！

members.note: Before a time or an event, or alone: in the past (我以前住在北京).

examples.text: 他总是跟我们说以前的故事。
看着以前的自己，我笑了起来。
两三个星期以前我去香港旅游。

members.note: Long ago; never after another word; the opening of a story.

groups.text: All three mean before. 以前 and 之前 follow a time or an event (Event + 以前/之前), and alone mean before now; 之前 is a little more formal and often marks the short time just before. 从前 always stands alone, for the distant past, as in stories.

members.note: After a time or an event, past or future; alone: in the future (以后再说).

examples.text: 你以后再也不会看到它了。
一个月以后，他少了三公斤。
新年以后，我们班级去公园玩。

members.note: After a time or an event; a little more formal than 以后.

examples.text: 之后，广告结束了。
他们四十分钟之后下课。
见过他之后我就去东京了。

members.note: Afterwards, later on: only for past events, never after another word.

examples.text: 后来，她又把这个方法教给了我妈妈。
后来，妈妈用她的手机给我的手机打电话。
后来鸡大了，叫的声音也大了，邻居们都不高兴。

members.note: Then, the next step of a sequence; links clauses, often after 先.

examples.text: 然后我去学校学习汉语。
然后我给她做饭，还给她读报纸。
我先到北京，然后坐火车到兰州。

groups.text: 以后 and 之后 follow a time or an event (Event + 以后/之后) and can point to the future; 以后 alone means from now on. 后来 means later on, only about the past, and stands alone. 然后 links steps in order: 先 A, 然后 B.

members.note: Again, already happened, or certain to come, often before 要, 能 or 是 (明天又是星期一); 又…又… means both … and ….

examples.text: 又开始下雨了。
今天他又迟到了。
我希望不久以后你又能好起来。

members.note: Again, not yet happened; also then, afterwards (先…再…).

examples.text: 我很想再见他们。
我说，我们下个月再到这里来。
来，再试试看。

groups.text: Both mark a repeat. 又 is for a repeat that has happened (他又来了), or one that is certain to come, often before 要, 能 or 是 (又要考试了). 再 is for a repeat still to come, in a request or a plan (请再说一遍), and also means then, once something else is done (吃了饭再走).

members.note: Distance from (学校离家很近); also the time left until something (离考试还有三天).

examples.text: 杭州离上海很近。
电影院离电车站近吗？
那儿离我学校不到公交一个站。

members.note: From: a starting place or time (从北京来, 从八点到十点).

examples.text: 她从家里跑了出来。
一个人是从香港来的姐姐。
我从西安坐火车来到成都。

groups.text: 离 measures the distance or time between two points: A 离 B + 远/近. 从 marks a starting point in space or time and is followed by a movement or by 到: 从 A 到 B. Use 离 for how far, 从 for where from.

members.note: Between or among people, places or times (朋友之间).

examples.text: 有时候是一次有趣的旅行，有时候是和朋友之间的误会。
你们俩之间是不是出现了什么问题？他怎么最近都不来接你了？
在牙齿之间等不容易刷到的地方可以使用牙线。

members.note: Within a limit of time, space or number (一个小时之内).

examples.text: 这10天之内我时而读古兰经时而做礼拜。

members.note: The middle, or in between; stands alone as a place word (坐在中间).

examples.text: 我在箱子里放了三件衬衫和一条裤子，电脑放在衣服中间。
在客厅的正中间的火盒加了暖和的气氛。
中间的区域是用于观察太阳和满月的升起。

groups.text: 之间 follows two or more things and means between or among them: A 和 B 之间. 之内 follows a period, an area or a limit and means within it: Time + 之内. 中间 is a place word, the middle or in between, which can also stand alone.

members.note: Continuously, without a break (一直下雨); also straight ahead (一直走).

examples.text: 三天一直下雨。
我要一直做下去。
他一直看我做的事。

members.note: Always: every time or nearly so; a habit.

examples.text: 鸡总是跟在我后面走。
他总是跟我们说以前的故事。
夏天天气热的时候，他总是穿着短裤在路边跑步。

members.note: Always, in speech, usually about something annoying.
From beginning to end, unchanged; more formal (始终没来).

examples.text: 在此后的几天，胡耀邦始终没有提出什么意见。
小时候，我一直梦想能弹钢琴，可是家里条件有限，这个愿望始终没有实现。

groups.text: 一直 is continuous: an action or state that has not stopped, and also straight on in one direction. 总是 is repeated: it happens on nearly every occasion. 老是 is like 总是 but spoken and usually a complaint. 始终 is from start to end without change, often with a negation.
